senses.definition: (uncountable) The act of offering (an idea) for consideration.
(countable) An idea, plan, or suggestion offered.

senses.definition: (countable, logic) The content of an assertion that may be taken as being true or false and is considered abstractly without reference to the linguistic sentence that constitutes the assertion; (Aristotelian logic) a predicate of a subject that is denied or affirmed and is connected by a copula.
examples: “Wiktionary is a good dictionary” is a proposition.

senses.definition: (countable, mathematics, philosophy) An assertion so formulated that it can be considered true or false.
(countable, mathematics) An assertion which is provably true, but not important enough to be called a theorem.
A statement of religious doctrine; an article of faith; a creed.
examples: the propositions of Wyclif and Huss
